newsitem.title: USA: YPF SA note sale seen postponed until 1997.
newsitem.headline: YPF SA note sale seen postponed until 1997.

text.p: YPF SA, an Argentine oil and gas company, is said to have postponed its Yankee offering of $200 million in debt until sometime in 1997, market sources said.
Earlier Thursday, other sources said YPF had delayed the deal due to unfavorable market conditions.

A syndicate official familiar with the offering speculated that YPF, which has a solid reputation among U.S. investors, was likely to have sought aggressive pricing on its issue. The company may have been stymied by a recent correction in emerging markets debt, he added.
The official said spreads on emerging market debt have widened significantly recently, following a bull market which lasted about three to four months.
"It's been a tough market for emerging market issues recently. There's been a hell of a correction.
"YPF would have wanted anything from 50 to 100 basis points through (Argentine) sovereigns. That may have been hard to get," the syndicate source added.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc was the lead manager of the offering of B1/BB-minus non-callable senior medium-term notes due 2001. Merrill officials declined to comment.
